newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco stocks get lift from Florida court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco stocks get lift from Florida court ruling.

text.p: Tobacco stocks jumped in early U.S. trading on Tuesday, lifted by news a judge dismissed pre-1994 claims in a Medicaid lawsuit brought against the industry by the state of Florida.

"It's like these stocks have been through a very bad storm and now you're beginning to see the sky brighten a bit," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, a money management firm that owns shares of tobacco giant Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Philip Morris, one of the Dow 30, was up 2-1/8 to 94-1/8.
RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, parent of R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, gained 3/4 to 27-1/4. B.A.T Industries Plc , parent of Brown & Williamson, was up 3/4 to 14-1/2 in U.S. trading.
Loews Corp gained 3/8 to 79-1/8 and smokeless tobacco maker UST Inc was up 1-1/8 to 30-3/4.
In his decision, Circuit Judge Harold Cohen also threw out 15 of the state's 18 claims against the cigarette companies.
The judge ruled that a recent state Supreme Court decision held that those claims could not go forward under the 1994 Florida Medicaid Amendments.
